title: Understanding Effects of Crystalline Structure on Electrical Properties of W/Ge0.15Te0.85/W Ovonic Threshold Switch with Local Biasing System by Conductive Atomic Force Microscope
content: The explosive development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology requires memory technologies to handle massively parallel data. 3D phase change memory, called 3D Xpoint memory, is considered as the most promising candidate for next-generation memory architecture. Although its outstanding storage capacity, commercialization of this architecture is challenging due to undesired current, called sneak current, caused by narrow distance between cells that can induce crosstalk. To address this issue, introducing selectors between memory cell and electrode is suggested, and many types of selectors have been researched over the past few decades. Among various selectors, chalcogenide-based Ovonic Threshold Switch (OTS) has attracted interest due to high drive current, nanosecond switching speed, low leakage current, and high endurance [1].
